bull.b: Affirm’s shift from negative operating cash flow to substantial positive generation improves its ability to fund growth, support lending activity, and reduce reliance on external financing. Free cash flow near $1 billion also provides durable capacity to invest in products and merchant expansion.

The materially lower leverage and larger equity base strengthen Affirm’s financial flexibility as a lending and payments platform. A better-capitalized balance sheet can support funding needs, absorb credit variability, and provide more room to pursue strategic investments over the coming quarters.

Growth across Pay-in-X, Affirm Card, and merchant distribution indicates expanding engagement with both consumers and commerce partners. Broader product adoption can deepen checkout integration, increase transaction opportunities, and diversify growth beyond a single installment product.

bear.b: A sharp annual revenue contraction and inconsistent profitability metrics reduce confidence that recent earnings improvement represents a stable operating trend. If revenue mix or recognition changes are driving the volatility, forecasting durable growth and margins becomes more difficult for the next several quarters.

Persistent implementation and checkout friction can slow Affirm’s expansion from online commerce into physical retail. Delayed offline adoption would limit the addressable transaction base, require continued engineering effort, and make merchant conversion and consumer usage gains less predictable.

Reliance on ABS timing and gain-on-sale economics can make reported revenue and earnings uneven even when underlying customer activity is healthy. Tax-rate fluctuations add another source of uncertainty, complicating planning and reducing visibility into recurring profitability over the medium term.
